gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.intro: A 60-second tour of what Work Calendar does and how to log in.

steps.1: Owners create a business at sign-up. Workers and managers join via an invite link from their owner.
steps.2: Use email + password, or Google sign-in if your owner has enabled it. 2FA can be turned on per account.
steps.3: Your role determines what you see: workers land on a personal home screen, owners and managers on the calendar.
steps.4: Pick your language (English, Dutch, French) in Settings → Profile so dates and labels match your team.

calendar.title: The calendar
calendar.intro: The shared calendar shows every shift colour-coded by status. It works on phone, tablet and desktop.

steps.1: Switch views with the toolbar: month, week, day, or list. Use arrow keys for fast navigation.
steps.2: Click a shift to open the details panel: who is assigned, applications, attendance, and chat.
steps.3: Colours: open shifts are blue, pending applications amber, filled shifts green, cancelled grey.
steps.4: Workers see only published shifts; owners and managers also see drafts and unpublished ones.

calendar.tip: Hold Shift while clicking to multi-select shifts on the planner — useful with the bulk-operations buttons.

myHome.title: Your home screen (/me)
myHome.intro: A mobile-first dashboard with everything you need before a shift.

steps.1: The big hero card shows your next shift, with the start time, role, location and a relative countdown.
steps.2: Clock in becomes active 15 minutes before the shift starts and disappears once you've ended the shift.
steps.3: Stat tiles surface pending applications, unread notifications and the hours scheduled this week.
steps.4: Open broadcasts appear at the top — tap Accept to claim an open shift on a first-come basis.

availability.title: Setting your availability
availability.intro: Tell your owner when you can work so they don't have to guess.

steps.1: On /me, use the 14-day strip to mark days you're available between 09:00 and 17:00 with a single tap.
steps.2: For other time windows, open the calendar, click an empty slot, and choose 'Set availability'.
steps.3: Use availability templates (under Settings if your owner enabled them) for recurring patterns like weekends.

availability.tip: Updating availability does not auto-apply to shifts — you still pick what you want to work.

applications.title: Applying for shifts
applications.intro: Pick the shifts you want to work and wait for owner approval.

steps.1: Click any open shift in the calendar and choose 'Apply'. You'll see your application status in real time.
steps.2: Pending applications appear on /me and on the dedicated /applications page.
steps.3: You can withdraw a pending application at any time. Once approved, you must use a shift swap to step away.

swaps.title: Shift swaps
swaps.intro: Hand a confirmed shift to a colleague when something comes up.

steps.1: Open the shift in the calendar and pick 'Offer swap'. Choose a colleague from the eligibility list.
steps.2: The recipient gets a notification. If they accept, the assignment moves; you both see the change in real time.
steps.3: Owners and managers see every swap in the audit log, and may decline a swap that breaks scheduling rules.

broadcasts.title: Open-shift broadcasts
broadcasts.intro: Fill a last-minute hole by asking every eligible worker at once.

steps.1: Owners and managers: open an under-staffed shift and click 'Broadcast'. Everyone with the right skills is notified.
steps.2: Workers: a broadcast lands as a push notification and at the top of /me with an Accept button.
steps.3: First Accept wins atomically — no double bookings even if multiple workers tap at the same instant.

timeClock.title: Time clock
timeClock.intro: Record actual start and end times so payroll matches reality.

steps.1: Workers: from /clock or /me, tap 'Clock in' once you've started, and 'Clock out' at the end.
steps.2: If you forget, your owner can edit the entry afterwards. The original timestamps are preserved in the audit log.
steps.3: Owners and managers approve time entries on /clock; only approved entries flow into payroll exports.

timeOff.title: Time off
timeOff.intro: Request days off and have the schedule respect them automatically.

steps.1: Workers: go to /timeoff, pick a date range and a reason. Conflicts with existing shifts are flagged immediately.
steps.2: Owners and managers approve or reject from the same page. Approved time off blocks new assignments in that range.
steps.3: Scheduling rules treat approved time off as a hard no-go: AI suggestions and bulk operations skip those days.

documents.title: Documents (ID, contracts, certificates)
documents.intro: Keep papers like your ID, work contract, and food-safety certificate in one place.

steps.1: On Settings → Profile, drag a PDF or photo (max 10 MB) into the dropzone, or click to choose a file.
steps.2: Pick the document type and the expiry date if there is one. Only you and your business owner can see it.
steps.3: Documents expiring within 30 days surface as warnings on the worker profile page.
steps.4: Storage is optional — if your owner hasn't set up S3/R2, the section is hidden automatically.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.intro: Three channels: in-app, web push, and email. You control what comes through.

steps.1: The bell icon in the header shows unread items. Click any notification to jump to the related shift or request.
steps.2: Enable push notifications on Settings → Profile to get alerts on your phone or laptop, even with the tab closed.
steps.3: Email preferences are per-event (invites, shift reminders, approvals) on the same settings page.

icsFeed.title: Calendar subscription (ICS)
icsFeed.intro: Your Work Calendar shifts in Google, Apple or Outlook calendar — always up to date.

steps.1: On Settings → Profile, copy your personal calendar URL.
steps.2: Paste it into your calendar app as a new subscription (don't import — it would be a one-off snapshot).
steps.3: If a device is lost or shared by mistake, click 'Revoke and rotate URL' to invalidate the old link instantly.

icsFeed.tip: Don't share the URL — it contains a signed token that lets anyone with the link see your schedule.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.intro: Name, phone, language, security and contact preferences.

steps.1: Update your display name, phone and language at any time. Changes apply immediately.
steps.2: Change your password from the same page; current password is required for safety.
steps.3: Two-factor authentication adds a TOTP code from any authenticator app — strongly recommended for owners.

workersDirectory.title: Workers directory
workersDirectory.intro: Manage who is on your team, their roles, skills and status.

steps.1: Invite a worker by email from /workers. They get a single-use link valid for 7 days.
steps.2: Click a worker to open their profile: hours, contract, skills, no-show rate, and expiring documents.
steps.3: Suspend or reactivate workers without deleting their history. Suspended workers cannot apply or be assigned.
steps.4: Promote a worker to manager from their profile if you want them to plan shifts but not run the business.

shiftsPlanner.title: Shifts planner
shiftsPlanner.intro: Create, edit, and publish shifts from the calendar.

steps.1: Click an empty slot on the calendar or use 'New shift' for a precise dialog.
steps.2: Set role label, required spots, time range, optional location, and required skill.
steps.3: Shifts start as drafts. Workers only see them after you click 'Publish week' or publish individually.
steps.4: Drag a shift to move it; drag its edge to resize. Changes save automatically.
steps.5: Conflicts (over-capacity, overlap, time-off, weekly cap, rest period, age limits) are blocked with a clear error.

shiftsPlanner.tip: Create a roster template once for a typical week, then apply it onto any future week to skip repetitive setup.

bulkOps.title: Bulk operations
bulkOps.intro: Move many shifts at once for fast weekly planning.

steps.1: Duplicate this week: copies every shift in the current week as drafts into the next week.
steps.2: Cancel today: marks every shift starting today as cancelled. Workers see a strike-through and are notified.
steps.3: Bulk reschedule: select shifts and move them all by a fixed number of minutes. Refuses to move into the past.

aiSuggestions.title: AI staffing suggestions
aiSuggestions.intro: Rule-based ranking of who should fill an under-staffed shift.

steps.1: Open an unfilled shift; a suggestions panel shows the top workers with a score and reasons.
steps.2: Suggestions factor in availability, skills, weekly hours used, rest periods, and recent no-shows.
steps.3: Click 'Assign' on a suggestion to fill the spot directly without going through the apply / approve flow.

steps.1: Open a shift to see its pending applications, with each worker's hours so far and any skill match.
steps.2: Approve or reject with one click. The worker is notified instantly and the shift status updates everywhere.
steps.3: You cannot approve beyond the required spots — the system blocks it. Increase capacity first if needed.

attendance.title: Attendance marking
attendance.intro: Track who showed up, who was late, and who didn't make it.

steps.1: For any past shift, open the details panel and pick On time, Late, No-show or Excused per assignment.
steps.2: No-shows count towards the worker's 90-day no-show rate shown on their profile and on the insights dashboard.
steps.3: Repeated marking is allowed if you made a mistake — the audit log preserves the history.

skillsRoster.title: Skills and roster templates
skillsRoster.intro: Reusable building blocks for fast scheduling.

steps.1: Define skills (bar, kitchen, host, etc.) under Settings → Skills, with a colour code.
steps.2: Tag each shift with a required skill so only qualified workers can apply.
steps.3: Roster templates under Settings → Rosters capture a whole week of shifts to apply onto future weeks in one click.

insights.title: Insights dashboard
insights.intro: A weekly view of how your business is doing.

steps.1: /insights shows shifts published, hours scheduled, fill rate and no-show rate per week.
steps.2: Compare weeks side by side to spot understaffed days or unusual no-show spikes.
steps.3: All numbers are computed live from the data you already have — there's nothing to configure.

payroll.title: Payroll export
payroll.intro: Export approved hours for your provider.

steps.1: On /payroll/time-entries pick a date range and a provider preset (SD Worx, Securex, or generic).
steps.2: Only approved time entries are included. Anything pending is highlighted so you don't ship incomplete data.
steps.3: Download a CSV ready to upload to your provider's portal.

dimona.title: Belgian Dimona declarations
dimona.intro: Automatic ONSS Dimona OUT/IN declarations when shifts start.

steps.1: Enter your Dimona credentials once under Settings → Developers (they're encrypted at rest).
steps.2: Set DIMONA_ENV to sandbox to test against ONSS without real declarations, then switch to prod when ready.
steps.3: Declarations run automatically; reconciliation jobs retry failures and surface them on /audit.

dimona.tip: Keep DIMONA_ENV on 'mock' in development — it logs intended declarations but doesn't hit ONSS.

messaging.title: Shift chat
messaging.intro: Quick messages tied to a specific shift.

steps.1: Inside the shift detail panel, scroll to the chat box. All assigned workers and managers can read and write.
steps.2: Use it for last-minute info (dress code, entry instructions) instead of a separate WhatsApp group.
steps.3: Messages are kept as long as the shift exists; deleting the shift removes the chat with it.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.intro: Searchable history of every meaningful action in your business.

steps.1: Filter by user, action type, free-text query or date range to find a specific change.
steps.2: Every create / update / delete on shifts, assignments, time-off, attendance and settings is recorded.
steps.3: Logs are kept indefinitely — useful for GDPR requests and resolving disputes.

developers.title: Developers — API keys & webhooks
developers.intro: Build integrations on top of your business data.

steps.1: Create API keys with the smallest set of scopes (shifts:read, shifts:write, …) for each integration.
steps.2: Send Idempotency-Key headers on POST requests to safely retry without creating duplicates.
steps.3: Subscribe webhooks to events like shift.created and shift.cancelled. Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256.
steps.4: Browse the full OpenAPI document at /api/v1/openapi to see every endpoint, schema and rate limit.

developers.tip: Rate limits are per key: 600 reads/minute and 120 writes/minute. Anything beyond returns 429 with Retry-After.

settings.title: Business settings
settings.intro: Locations, billing details, and operational defaults.

steps.1: Add multiple locations if you run more than one venue; each shift can be tagged with one.
steps.2: Set business-wide scheduling defaults (min rest, weekly cap, minor age limit) once instead of per shift.
steps.3: GDPR tools let you export or fully delete any user's data on /me/data.

steps.1: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. 2FA uses standard TOTP — pair with any authenticator app.
steps.2: Sensitive credentials (Dimona) are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and never logged in plaintext.
steps.3: Every privileged action is logged. Lost a device? Revoke the calendar URL and reset your password from Settings.
